authority: Owner ruling, post-architecture assurance-closure campaign (2026-10-14): ASM-0069 approved exactly as it exists on main 72127a07; the wording change from 'clamped skew' to bounded `MaxClockSkew` and from 'skew clamp' to 'skew's type' reflects the already-approved refusal semantics of MCPRE-200/#1125; scope, premise class, boundary, description and semantics unchanged
text:
[[assumption]]
id = "ASM-0069"
description = "The wall-clock `now` handed to the delegated-credential chain check is the verifying party's current UTC time, to within the deployment's configured skew of the issuer's clock."
justification = """
`http_profile.delegated_credential_chain` admits a credential only inside its own `nbf`/`exp`
window, widened by the bounded `MaxClockSkew` (`check_freshness`). The chain holds no clock: `now` is an
argument to every verifier operation, supplied by whoever verifies the response — the client
proxy's verification clock, an SDK caller, or, for a retained exchange, the instant at which
the exchange was retained. So the conclusion *this credential is inside its window* is a
conclusion about the instant the chain was GIVEN, and it is a conclusion about the present only
if that value is the present. Nothing in this repository can establish that: the reading comes
from a host clock disciplined by whatever the verifying party runs.

This is the per-unit counterpart of ASM-0057 and does not widen it. ASM-0057 states what the
serving path hands the request-side verifier operations, scoped to `http_profile.freshness_window`
and `http_profile.admission_currency`; the delegated chain is a response-side check fed by a
different party's clock, and widening an owner-reviewed premise to a consumer it was not written
for would reopen its review for the units it already serves.

A clock that steps backwards re-admits a credential whose `exp` has passed, and one that steps
forwards refuses a credential that is current; both are the same failure of this premise and
neither is detectable from one response. The skew's type bounds how far a misconfigured
TOLERANCE can widen the window; it says nothing about a wrong READING.

It stops being acceptable if the chain is ever handed a value that is not an acquisition of the
verifying host's wall clock (or, for a retained exchange, the instant recorded when it was
retained), or if the chain gains a clock of its own.
"""
scope = [
  "unit://http_profile.delegated_credential_chain",
  "boundary://boundary.clock",
]
owner = "mats@sundvall.name"
introduced_by = "owner-signature:tcb-os-entropy-premise (r12, b243d21bc1720a78, clock half)"
review_requirement = "Owner review if the delegated-credential window is judged against any value other than the verifying party's wall-clock reading, or if the chain gains a clock of its own."
premise_class = "external-boundary"
boundary_owner = """
The operator of the VERIFYING host's clock discipline (NTP or equivalent), across the wall-clock
acquisition that supplies `now` to a delegated-response verification: the reading is the current
UTC time to within the configured skew of the issuer's clock.
"""
affected_contracts = []
sites = [
  "mcp-re-http-profile/src/delegation/verify.rs#check_freshness",
]
tool_specific_mechanism = "none:trusted-seam"
